heroHeadline: 78th Nakba Day: Ben Gvir Raises Flag on Temple Mount; Netanyahu Files NYT Lawsuit Over Palestinian Sexual Violence Report; Saudi Arabia Reaffirms No Israel Normalization Without Palestinian State
heroSubtitle: On the 78th anniversary of Israeli independence and Palestinian Nakba Day (May 14, 2026), National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir ascended the Temple Mount and raised an Israeli flag next to the Dome of the Rock ahead of Jerusalem Day celebrations — his fifth documented 2026 incursion into Haram al-Sharif. MK Yitzhak Kroizer of Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party called for demolishing the mosques and building the Third Temple; Jordan condemned the visit as a 'dangerous provocation that inflames religious sentiments.' Simultaneously, PM Netanyahu announced a defamation lawsuit against the New York Times and columnist Nicholas Kristof over a May 13 op-ed documenting allegations of sexual violence by Israeli soldiers and interrogators against Palestinian detainees — calling it a 'blood libel.' Saudi Arabia publicly reaffirmed during Trump's Middle East tour that no normalization with Israel is possible without Palestinian statehood, directly contradicting Trump's February claim that Riyadh had dropped that precondition. In Washington, a third round of direct Israel-Lebanon talks began at the State Department. The IDF killed one Palestinian operative crossing the ceasefire line in northern Gaza, bringing the post-ceasefire Palestinian death toll to approximately 885+. The Netanyahu coalition's Knesset dissolution bill, filed May 13, awaits a preliminary vote the week of May 18 — with elections expected by mid-October 2026.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
